name: Peter Navarro
role: American economist and White House trade adviser in the first and second Trump administrations
summary: Navarro advocates protective tariffs, industrial onshoring, economic separation from China and strict immigration enforcement. His later speeches oppose major green industrial policies and allege partisan misuse of government, while his earlier record includes environmental and abortion-rights advocacy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Made deregulation a central plank of economic growth.

abortion-legal.rationale: His recorded congressional-campaign position supported abortion choice; no later explicit legal position found.

more-religion-public.rationale: Urged pastors to mobilize congregations politically from their pulpits.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Explicitly proposed drastically reducing Chinese student and researcher visas.

free-trade.rationale: Rejected unconditional free-trade claims under nonreciprocal trading rules.

nation-first.rationale: Prioritized American wages, industry and security over prevailing global-trade arrangements.

open-borders.rationale: Defended deterrence, deportation and employer enforcement against unlawful immigration.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Condemned the Green New Deal approach as destructive to American industry.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Praised expansion of nuclear-fuel recycling and enrichment as strategic industrial investment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Explicitly defended tariffs to rebuild American manufacturing.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed financial and tax incentives for strategic industrial onshoring.

political-violence-never.rationale: Presented Allied military victory over Nazi Germany and imperial Japan as necessary and admirable.

military-superiority.rationale: Welcomed American naval strategic dominance and opposed Chinese military ascendancy.

taxation-theft.rationale: Defended tariff revenues as legitimate public revenue rather than rejecting all taxation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Condemned large fiscal stimulus overspends and prioritized debt reduction.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Explicitly celebrated fracking and increased American energy production.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Alleged a shadow government and partisan officials concealed election interference.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Advocated active tariff protection and industrial incentives beyond basic security and property enforcement.

space-expansion.rationale: Advocated permanent lunar presence, deep-space industry and sustained outward exploration as national priorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sought reciprocal international exchange, not a completely closed bloc.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Proposed banning Chinese investment in strategic technology industries.

corporate-influence.rationale: Condemned lavish political contributions protecting offshoring and cheap labor.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Demanded closing Confucius Institutes as foreign-government influence operations.

non-intervention.rationale: Praised American action excluding rival powers from Venezuela and Cuba, alongside regional naval dominance.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned imprisonment for political disagreement and claimed partisan prosecution.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Defended military readiness and the industrial capacity to supply wars and allies.

pollution-taxes.rationale: His earlier writings explicitly endorsed taxes on carbon, gasoline and oil imports.

capital-controls.rationale: Proposed restrictions on Chinese investment and American portfolio flows.

voter-id.rationale: Urged passage of legislation restoring voter identification and citizenship safeguards.

close-ties-china.rationale: Recommended economic and financial decoupling from China.

notes: Latest clear trade views supersede earlier free-trade advocacy. The later Green New Deal criticism is recorded alongside an earlier specific carbon-tax endorsement; no explicit later carbon-tax retraction was found. His 2020 climate interview avoided the issue rather than clearly retracting his prior scientific position. No social or constitutional positions inferred from other Project 2025 chapters, party membership or Trump’s policies. Carson’s Christian-national identity claims at the faith event are not Navarro’s. His Green Bay Sweep sought to reject certified 2020 results through Congress and state legislatures; he claimed legality and said violence disrupted it. This controversy does not automatically establish a view on every constitutional-design statement. His fraud and foreign-interference allegations are his assertions, not validated findings. Advocacy of alternative statutory tariff powers after a Supreme Court defeat does not establish opposition to separate branches or unlimited presidential authority. Balanced trade is not an explicit trade-surplus goal. Visa reduction concerns a specific nationality and category; no racial hierarchy inferred. General complaints about gender indoctrination do not identify a specific gender-identity or sex-education law. Remaining nulls reviewed across ten themes.
